The '''1744 [[FLLA]] World Cup''' was the 19th edition of the [[FLLA World Cup]], the quadrennial international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. It was held in [[Lycroa]] across [[Ayuma]], and was won by [[Lycroa]], who defeated [[Easuhura]] 0-0 ''(3-0 pens)'' in the final.

The 1744 tournament was the first held under the FLLA's '''confederation rotation policy''', adopted in 1742, and returned the World Cup to [[Ayuma]] for the first time since the [[1736 FLLA World Cup|1736 edition]]. [[Lycroa]] hosted and lifted the trophy for the fifth time, defeating [[Easuhura]] in a goalless final settled by a 3-0 penalty shoot-out at the principal venue in Huifarn. The result extended Lycroa's record as the most successful side in the competition's history.
